extracted.intended_audience: Toastmasters contest chairs, chief judges, voting/tiebreaking judges, timers, ballot counters, contestants, and contest organizers
extracted.subtask_description: Official rulebook guidance for planning, conducting, judging, timing, recording, protesting, and submitting entries for Toastmasters speech contests (club through international levels), including specialized rules for International, Evaluation, Humorous, Table Topics, Tall Tales, Online, Video, and Video Speech contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot completion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a ballot to be valid, judges shall complete their ballots by entering their choices for first, second, and third place and sign and print their names. E-signatures are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot submission and handling (voting judges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting judges must discreetly provide the bottom portion of the ballot to the ballot counters; the top portion is not provided and must be discreetly discarded by the voting judge after the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using physical ballots, provide voting judges with envelopes in which to secure their ballots prior to collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot submission and handling (tiebreaking judge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tiebreaking judge ranks all contestants in order, then discreetly provides the bottom portion of their ballot to the chief judge; the top portion is not provided and must be discreetly discarded by the tiebreaking judge after the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using physical ballots, provide the tiebreaking judge with an envelope in which to secure their ballot prior to collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Record Sheet handling
rubrics_metrics.description: As voting judges and the tiebreaking judge complete ballots, the timer with the stopwatch completes the Time Record Sheet and provides it to the chief judge, secured if physical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a physical form, provide the timer with an envelope in which to secure the Time Record Sheet prior to collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private tabulation of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all ballots are collected, ballot counters and the chief judge tabulate results in a private counting room (physical or virtual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Counter’s Tally Sheet (Item 1176) for tabulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring points per ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Counter's Tally Sheet, each first-place ranking scores 3 points, second-place 2 points, and third-place 1 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once all points are entered, compute total points for each contestant and enter totals on the bottom of the tally sheet; point totals must be verified by all ballot counters before results are entered on the sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking and tie resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants are ranked by total points; in the event of a tie the chief judge consults the tiebreaking judge’s ballot; the tied contestant who received the highest ranking on the tiebreaking judge’s ballot gains the contested place, others ranked behind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and results forms
rubrics_metrics.description: After tabulation, the chief judge completes the Notification of Contest Winner form (Item 1182) and the Results Form (Item 1168) with required information and submits to the contest chair or next-level contest chair as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of Contest Winner uses ranking of all contestants; Results Form lists winners in reverse order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and destruction of ballots and records
rubrics_metrics.description: All ballots and the tally sheet are kept by the chief judge until after winners have been announced, after which the chief judge will destroy all ballots, the time record, and the tally sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of winners order and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are announced in reverse order (third, second, first). In contests with fewer than three participants announce second (if applicable) then first. Winners must be announced prior to the end of the event or before the contest adjourns; if multiple contests at an event, winners from all contests must be announced before the end of the conference/event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple contests are taking place at one event, each contest must be officially adjourned prior to beginning the next contest, even if winners have not yet been announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement specifics for international quarterfinals/semifinals
rubrics_metrics.description: For International Speech Contest Quarterfinals and Semifinals advancing contestants will be announced in no particular order; placement will not be announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and correction of winner announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcement of contest winners is final unless the list was announced incorrectly, in which case chief judge, ballot counters, or timers may immediately interrupt to correct the error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timers appointment and devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Two timers are appointed by the chief judge: one with a stopwatch, the other with a signaling device showing green/yellow/red; for Online contests at least one backup timer is also appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signaling device must be in full view of each contestant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official timing record
rubrics_metrics.description: The stopwatch timer maintains and delivers the written record of elapsed time on the Speech Contest Time Record Sheet (Item 1175); this constitutes the official time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and accuracy of signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: The timer managing the signaling device ensures contestants can view accurate green/yellow/red signals at appropriate times during the speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No signal can be given for the overtime period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech timing windows and disqualification thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Each contest type has required speech length windows and disqualification thresholds (International/Humorous/Online 5–7 minutes; disqualify <4:30 or >7:30 with disqualification at 7:31; Table Topics 1–2 minutes; disqualify <1:00 or >2:30 with disqualification at 2:31; Evaluation 2–3 minutes; disqualify <1:30 or >3:30 with disqualification at 3:31; Tall Tales 3–5 minutes; disqualify <2:30 or >5:30 with disqualification at 5:31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must not consider fractions of a second. A contestant is not qualified until their lower threshold time is reached and not disqualified until the upper threshold plus one second is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing start protocol after introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being introduced, the contestant must proceed immediately to the speaking position and say 'Thank you, Contest Chair' to test audiovisual equipment; timing begins with the contestant's next definite verbal or nonverbal communication after the equipment check if equipment is functional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If audiovisual equipment is not functional the contest chair pauses to correct; for Online contests contestant is allowed 10 minutes to attempt corrections; if corrected the contestant is reintroduced; if unable to correct within 10 minutes contest continues with next contestant.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unnecessary delays by speaker
rubrics_metrics.description: The speaker should begin speaking within a short time after arriving at the speaking area and is not permitted to delay the contest unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning signal schedules by contest type
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific times for green/yellow/red signals vary by contest type—for International/Humorous/Online green at 5:00 (1 minute), yellow at 6:00 (1 minute), red at 7:00 until conclusion; Evaluation green at 2:00 (30s), yellow at 2:30 (30s), red at 3:00 until conclusion; Table Topics green at 1:00 (30s), yellow at 1:30 (30s), red at 2:00 until conclusion; Tall Tales green at 3:00 (1 min), yellow at 4:00 (1 min), red at 5:00 until conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all speech contests no signal can be given for overtime period; visually impaired contestants may request alternate signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodations for visually impaired contestants
rubrics_metrics.description: Visually impaired contestants may request and must be granted a warning signal of their choosing (e.g., buzzer, bell, or person announcing times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a special device or instructions are required the contestant must provide them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical failure overtime allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is technical failure of the signal or timing equipment, a speaker is allowed 30 seconds extra overtime before being disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of number of time disqualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to announcing results, the contest chair must announce the number of time disqualifications, but not name the contestant(s) involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests are limited to eligibility, originality, and reference to another contestant or another contestant’s speech and must be lodged only by voting judges and/or contestants prior to the contest being adjourned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest chair and chief judge must receive protests before adjournment; protests from audience members must not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond before disqualification for originality/reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Before disqualifying a contestant for originality or referencing another contestant’s speech, the contestant must be given an opportunity to respond to the voting judges; a majority of voting judges must concur to disqualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility disqualification authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest chair can disqualify a contestant on the basis of eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All decisions of voting judges and qualifying judges are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Props and electronic devices notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants who plan to use props (including electronic devices, music, PowerPoint, virtual backgrounds) must notify the contest chair prior to the contest and abide by venue restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All props must be set up during the minute of silence prior to the speech and removed during the minute of silence after the speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Props set-up demonstration and denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must demonstrate prior to the contest that props can be set up and removed in allotted times; if unable to demonstrate, props cannot be used during the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants may enlist someone to help with props, but contest officials are not responsible for assisting.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Speech Contest language and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: International Speech Contest must be conducted in English only and every speech should clearly develop and present ideas in a substantially original speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows General Rules with specified additions/exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-level video recording requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: District-level contest videos submitted for quarterfinal judging must have clear audio without echo/static; record in high definition; single-camera only; camera on tripod; unobstructed in-focus view of contestant; entire speaking area visible; camera monitored by an operator; no zooming; speaking area fully lit with visible facial expressions; no lighting pointed directly at camera; recording must contain only the introduction by contest chair and the entire winning speech; no editing allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet any recording requirement will result in contestant disqualification and notification to the submitting District.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterfinal video viewing protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarterfinal judges view assigned videos in the order provided, must view all videos in one sitting, may view each video only once, and pausing or rewinding is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for new speech at World Championship
rubrics_metrics.description: Every participant in the World Championship of Public Speaking must present an entirely new and different speech than the one presented during that year's semifinal or any previous year's semifinal/final contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semifinal winners prepare and deliver outlines of semifinal speech(s) to World Headquarters; qualifying judges receive outlines and a qualification sheet to indicate whether the World Championship speech is entirely new; qualifying judges complete qualification sheet and submit with ballots; if 3 of 5 qualifying judges mark Disqualified for a speaker, that speaker is disqualified and no protest may be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semifinals rulebook version
rubrics_metrics.description: The semifinals and World Championship follow the version of the rulebook that was in effect when the contest cycle began on the previous July 1 (approximately 14 months before the World Championship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Contest test speech and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of the Evaluation Contest a 5–7 minute test speech (contest-type or Pathways project) is presented; contestants have five minutes to prepare their evaluation using the Evaluation Contestant Notes sheet (Item 1177) and must hand notes in when preparation time ends; notes returned to contestants when introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test speaker's project/objectives must not be known to contestants, judges, or audience. Where impractical for contestants to leave the room, preparation occurs under control of Sergeant at Arms. Contestants must not use digital devices to gain unfair advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Contest introductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce each contestant by announcing the contestant’s name twice (Evaluation speeches do not have titles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended that the test speaker not be a member of the same club as any contestant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous Speech Contest content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Humorous Contest speech subject selected by contestant; speaker must avoid potentially objectionable language/anecdotes/material; speech must be thematic (opening, body, close), not a monologue/series of one-liners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table Topics single-topic and topic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All Table Topics contestants must receive the same topic of a general nature selected by the contest chair; topic must be of reasonable length, not require detailed knowledge, and lead to an opinion or conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants receive no advance knowledge; contestants must not use digital devices; when contest begins all contestants except first must leave room under Sergeant at Arms; introduce each contestant by announcing name, topic, topic, name; at conclusion next speaker invited into the room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tall Tales content and props
rubrics_metrics.description: Tall Tales speech subject must be highly exaggerated, improbable, and have a theme or plot; humor and props may be used to support or illustrate the speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Speech Contest live participation and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Online Speech Contest conducted with all contestants and officials participating live online from physically distant locations using participant-obtained equipment; all briefings and rehearsals conducted online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefings must include guidance on technical-difficulty handling, contact methods for chief judge/contest chair/moderators, and communication methods during contest. Rehearsal must include audiovisual check and defining each contestant's speaking area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online platform technical capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The selected online platform must allow contestants to turn video on/off and mute/unmute, allow contest officials to view contestant speeches live while maintaining confidentiality, allow host controls (mute/video) and ability to prompt participants, and allow contestants to receive timing signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online pause and privacy statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief judge and contest chair must establish a private way to communicate or signal to pause the contest; the Online Speech Contest Statement about privacy and recording must be read or posted and informs attendees that attendance consents to recording and use by Toastmasters International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement discharges Toastmasters International from claims arising from use/distribution of recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online technical difficulty handling for contestants
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contestant's audio/video is severely weakened or lost, chief judge and contest chair determine whether to pause; if paused the impacted contestant has up to 10 minutes to reestablish a secure connection; if reestablished within 10 minutes the contestant continues from the last heard word/sentence with no extra time allowance; if not, contest continues with next contestant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge technical difficulties in online contests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a voting judge cannot hear/see well enough to complete responsibilities they must notify the chief judge immediately and their ballot will not be included in final results; backup judges may be appointed and must judge entire contest but their ballot used only if a primary judge was unable to complete their role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timer technical difficulties and backup timer role
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timer cannot hear/see well enough they must notify the chief judge; the backup timer must time speeches but their Time Record Sheet will only be consulted from the point the primary timer was unable to complete their role; if only one backup timer they must also be ready to operate the signaling device if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pausing/rescheduling online contests for widespread technical failure
rubrics_metrics.description: If enough participants experience technical difficulties such that contest cannot proceed, chief judge and contest chair may pause; if paused it must be resumed within one hour or the remainder rescheduled. If resumed and a contestant was partway through their speech they continue from last heard word/sentence with no additional time; if rescheduled only contestants who have not yet presented will present at rescheduled contest, and those partway through may begin from start at rescheduled contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest officials must send all partially completed forms to the chief judge to be stored until rescheduled contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of external voting systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of external voting systems is prohibited in the Online Speech Contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Speech Contest eligibility and video requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of undistricted clubs may enter the Video Speech Contest (in English) following applicable Toastmasters rules; only one speech per club may be submitted. Video entry requirements echo District video rules: clear audio, single-camera, unobstructed in-focus view, camera mounted/secured, no zooming, fully lit speaking area, speaker visible and in frame throughout, no lighting pointed at camera, recording contains only contest chair intro and the entire winning speech, no editing allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be submitted with a Video Speech Contest Entry Form including a live URL and a completed Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality (Item 1183). Deadlines apply (e.g., received by World Headquarters by specified date/time). Speeches not meeting timing requirements will be reviewed by chief judge and may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run-off competitions and advancement for Video Speech Contest
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than 10 eligible video submissions are received separate run-off competitions can be held; each run-off will have no more than 10 contestants and, insofar as practical, equal numbers; top three from each run-off advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging and chief judge assignment for Video Speech Contest
rubrics_metrics.description: For each run-off and final level of Video Speech Contest, a minimum of five voting judges and one tiebreaking judge will be appointed; voting and tiebreaking judges must meet International Speech Contest judging eligibility; for Video Speech Contest the Immediate Past International President twice removed is chief judge (or delegate appointed if unavailable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting judges and tiebreaking judge will not be physically present for the Video Speech Contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timers for Video Speech Contest
rubrics_metrics.description: Timers are not appointed for the Video Speech Contest; speeches are timed at club level and verified when videos are reviewed for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speeches failing timing requirements will be reviewed by chief judge and if determined over/under time, the video submission will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest planning checklist responsibilities (Contest Chair)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest chair must plan the budget, arrange venue/online platform/AV equipment, conduct pre- and post-contest publicity, ensure bills are paid, verify speaker eligibility and familiarity with rules, ensure AV equipment works, brief chief judge/voting judges/timers/counters, ensure ballots are counted carefully, and present awards appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the chair may have a committee, the chair is ultimately responsible. Contest income/expenses should break even; entry fees to attend must be waived for contestants; contestants cannot be charged to compete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation tasks and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare contest logistics: budget, venue/time selection with proper Toastmasters officer, agenda, supplies/services, order/download certificates/trophies, access Toastmasters contest materials online (list of item numbers), select chief judge and communication method for pausing, appoint supporting roles (Sergeant at Arms, test speaker), notify contest officials and contestants of briefings (2–6 weeks prior), provide contestants an information packet (rulebook, contestant profile, Speaker’s Certification, platform training materials if online).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note about trademark violation: cannot put Toastmasters logo or the words 'Toastmasters' or 'Toastmasters International' on awards not purchased from World Headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestants’ briefing responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: At contestant briefing verify contestant presence and name pronunciation, review contest rules and Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality, review timing protocol and speaking area, determine speaking positions, and ensure contestants are comfortable with online platform if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For in-person contests speaking area may include lectern, tables, lighting, microphone, etc., and all contestants must have opportunity to test amplifying equipment before contest.
